description: What VivaPlan can change, vary and measure: field paths with units, forms of time series, state variables, metric building blocks, experiment format, examples, measured computing time and limits; section choices explains every value of a choice field with its label in the app. Without section a compact overview of the other sections; read the section you need. With plan the computing time is measured on that plan.

plan.description: Id of an open plan (p1, …) to measure the computing time on.

section.description: Part of the catalog; without: all sections.

name: describe
title: Catalog for AIs

description: Opens a VivaPlan project file (.vplan or an older .rplan) as a working copy in memory, brought up to the current format, and returns its id (p1, …) with an overview without values: period, number of persons and properties, notes of the update, number of check messages. Only the named file is read; folders are not searched. If the user released plan folders, only files inside them are opened. With new: true an empty plan without a file is opened, as «New» in the app: use it when the user wants to compute with their own figures and has no file; the answer lists the missing inputs, ask the user for them and never invent values. With example: true the example plan is opened, only to try out or demonstrate VivaPlan; never compute the user's own situation with its values.

example.description: Open the example plan (only to try out or demonstrate).

new.description: Open a new, empty plan without a file (for the user's own figures).

path.description: Path of the file (.vplan or .rplan); ~/ stands for the home folder.

name: plan_open
title: Open a plan

description: Reads the values of a section of an open plan (e.g. household, flows, wealth, pension, realestate, taxes, returns, withdrawal, scenarios) or of a single field by field path as in the check messages (household.persons.0.birth). Without section and path: the list of sections with their size. Shares are fractions (0.05 = 5 %), amounts are per year in the currency of the plan unless the field says otherwise.

path.description: Field path, dot separated, list entries by number from 0.

name: plan_get
title: Read part of a plan

description: Looks up the structure of the project file (JSON Schema with descriptions). Without arguments the sections with their description; with section the part of the schema with the definitions it uses; with definition a single definition. Units and the meaning of the fields in short: describe with section fields.

definition.description: Name of a definition of the schema (e.g. Person).

name: plan_schema
title: Structure of the project file

description: Checks an open plan as the app does: messages with severity (error, warning, info), section, field path and text. A plan with errors cannot be computed.
name: plan_validate
title: Check a plan

description: Lists the results computed in this session: id (r1, …), plan, tool, number of runs, main key figure. Results stay only in the memory of the server; the results of the desktop app are separate.
name: result_list
title: Results of the session

description: Details of a result of the session. view: summary (key figures and the result in words, default), yearly (one row per calendar year, nominal or real), events (events of the run), bands (wealth per year at the percentiles over all runs), variations (key figures per combination of the variations). With several runs percentile picks the run for yearly and events (0 worst, 1, 5, 50, 95, 99; default 50); the runs of the percentiles are ordered by the nominal end wealth, with real by the end wealth in today's purchasing power (the run of a percentile may differ). from and to limit the calendar years.

real.description: Values in today's purchasing power instead of nominal (yearly, bands); yearly and events take the run of the percentile in the real order.

name: result_get
title: Details of a result

description: Time series of the data library of the app (folder «Zeitreihen» of its data folder): file, currency, period, monthly or yearly, average returns of stocks and bonds and inflation. Plans refer to them as library:<file>.
name: library_list
title: Data library

description: Simulates an open plan as the desktop app does: according to its source of returns (fixed, historical, rolling, bootstrap, parametric; returns.source) and with the variations stored in the plan. To choose the source by its label in the app («Monte Carlo · historisch» is bootstrap, «Alle historischen Startzeitpunkte» is rolling) read describe with section choices first. Returns the id of the result (r1, …), the key figures, the result in words and the estimate of the duration. First the duration is estimated; from 60 s nothing is computed without confirm: true (the answer then gives the estimate). Long computations report progress and can be cancelled. Details afterwards with result_get (yearly, events, bands, variations). To compare changes or search for better values use evaluate.

confirm.description: Compute even if the estimate is 60 s or more. Set it only after the user agreed to the duration.

paths.description: Number of paths for this run only (sources bootstrap and parametric).

name: simulation_run
title: Simulate a plan

description: Computes an experiment on an open plan in one call: changes by field path (set), variations as a grid or a pattern search (vary), metrics, constraints and an objective; the ranking of the variants comes with values on independent confirmation paths. This is the way to optimize and to compare variants. The format of the experiment: describe with section experiment. The plan itself stays unchanged. First the duration is estimated; from 60 s nothing is computed without confirm: true (status needsConfirmation with the estimate). Long computations report progress and can be cancelled.

confirm.description: Compute even if the estimate is 60 s or more. Set it only after the user agreed to the duration.

experiment.description: The experiment (set, vary, metrics, constraints, objective, search, budget).

name: evaluate
title: Experiment on a plan

description: Changes values of the working copy by field path as in the check messages (wealth.stockShare, household.persons.0.birth); a step of a course over time with path@<milestone id>, path@age:<years> or path@YYYY-MM. All changes of a call are one step: if one path or type is wrong, none is made. Answers every changed field with old and new value and the check messages afterwards. Nothing is written to a file; plan_undo takes the step back, plan_save saves.

changes.description: List of {path, value}; value as JSON (number, text, true/false, object).

name: plan_set
title: Change values

description: Lists all differences of the working copy against the file as it was opened or last saved: field path, value in the file, current value; with the number of steps plan_undo can take back.
name: plan_changes
title: Changes against the file

description: Takes back the last step of plan_set or plan_apply, with all: true all steps. Answers the values restored and the steps left.
name: plan_undo
title: Undo

description: Takes over a variant of an evaluate result into the plan it was computed from: the fixed values of the experiment (set) and the values of the variant with the rank given (1 = best), as one step like plan_set. The variations of the plan itself stay as they are.

rank.description: Rank of the variant in the result; default 1.

name: plan_apply
title: Take over a variant

description: Saves the working copy as a project file (.vplan). Without path and overwrite a new file next to the opened one (<name> (AI).vplan, with a number if needed); an existing file is never touched. path saves to another new file in the folder of the plan or a folder released with --allow-dir; a file name alone is enough. A plan without a file (new or example plan) is saved in the first released plan folder, so give only a file name such as `My plan.vplan`; ~/ stands for the home folder. overwrite: true replaces an existing file, but only after the program asked the user and showed the changes; a backup <file>.bak is kept, a file changed since opening and old .rplan files are never replaced. Answers the file name written.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file (asks the user first).

path.description: File to write (.vplan). A file name alone is enough: it is saved in the folder of the plan, for a plan without a file (new or example plan) in the first released plan folder. ~/ stands for the home folder.

name: plan_save
title: Save a plan
